4469.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷinumi, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey- (“to pay”). Cognate with ποινή (poinḗ), Sanskrit चयते (cáyate) and Avestan 𐬗𐬌𐬐𐬀𐬫𐬀𐬝 (cikayat̰).

4442.t: From συν- (sŭn-, “together”) + χύσις (khŭ́sĭs, “pouring”), or from συγχέω (sŭnkhéō, “to pour together, confound, trouble”) + -σις (-sĭs).

4451.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”). The unaspirated first consonant is due to Grassmann's law.

4465.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tr-ey-gʷ-, from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to rub”). Cognate with Latin tero.

4400.t: Unknown. The cluster /stʰ/ is unusual for Ancient Greek terms inherited from Proto-Indo-European.

4415.t: From Proto-Hellenic *stōyyā́, from Proto-Indo-European *stoh₂-w-ih₂, ultimately from the root *steh₂- (“to stand”), whence also στῦλος (stûlos, “column, pillar”).

4483.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰā́mā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-meh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂- (“to speak”). By surface analysis, a full-grade deverbal of φημί (phēmĭ́, “to say; to explain; to argue”).

4472.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰen-, albeit with no certain adduced cognates.

4485.t: From a case form of Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm (“earth”) (whence also χθών (khthṓn, “earth”)), traditionally taken as a dative.

4450.t: The suffix -ιγγ- implies a Pre-Greek origin because of non-native pronunciation.

4417.t: From στέλλω (stéllō, “to send”) + -ος (-os). See also στολή (stolḗ).

4449.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dʰeyh₂-? Proto-Indo-European *dʰyeh₂- Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Indo-European *dʰyéh₂mn̥ Proto-Hellenic *tsā́mə? Ancient Greek σῆμα Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *dʰyéh₂mn̥, from *dʰyeh₂- (“to notice”) (see…

4490.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰrṓwmə, and related to χρώς (khrṓs, “surface of the body, skin (color)”); see there for more.

4489.t: Nominal formation from the root of χράομαι (khráomai), χρεώ (khreṓ, “to need”), and χρή (khrḗ, “have to, ought”); see the latter for more.

4463.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *trewH-p-, a p-extension of a putative *trewH- (“to rub”), and cognate with τρύω (trúō, “to wear down”) and Proto-Slavic *tryti (“to rub”).

4410.t: According to Beekes, a Proto-Indo-European *th₂eys- (“dough”), whence also Proto-Slavic *těsto (“dough”), Old Irish táis (“dough”), and Old English þǣsma (“leaven”), with an influence from στέαρ (stéar, “fat”).

4422.t: From σύμμαχος (súmmakhos, “fighting with”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix).

4419.t: From στέγω (stégō, “to cover”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

4484.t: Per Rix (LIV), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂-n (“to yawn, to gape”) with inchoative suffix -σκω (-skō).

4495.t: From earlier *ἀϝάω (*ăwắō), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewh₂-, though without obvious cognates.

4497.t: From a root *ἀγαν- (*agan-) of uncertain origin plus a suffix -ακτέω (-aktéō, expressive formation suffix), as seen also in ὑλακτέω (hŭlaktéō, “to bark”).

4498.t: From a suffixed derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- (“to curve, bend”), whence also ἄγκος (ánkos, “bend”), ἀγκύλος (ankúlos, “curved, bent”).

4407.t: Uncertain. Often derived from σκάλλω (skállō, “to stir, hoe”) or from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelh₃p-, from *(s)kelh₃- (“to cut”), and so related to Latin scalpō (“to scratch”), English shelf and Lithuanian sklempti (“to plane”).

4418.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂mn̥ (“that which stands, stature”). Cognate with Latin stāmen (“warp of a loom; thread hanging from a distaff”).

4492.t: Uncertain but perhaps related to ψάλιον (psálion, “curb chain”) and ψέλιον (psélion, “armlet”). Maybe from Pre-Greek.

4494.t: The word is related to similar words meaning "foxes", like ψειαί (pseiaí), ψίαι (psíai), φοῦαι (phoûai) and φύλλες (phúlles). These variations cannot be all understood in Indo-European terms.

4480.t: From φύω (phúō, “to grow, to be . . . by nature”) + -η (-ē, nominal suffix).

4482.t: From φαίνω (phaínō, “to bring to light, to cause to appear”) + -μα (-ma, nominal suffix) with -σ- from analogy to other -αίνω : -ασμα or from φάσις (phásis).

4455.t: Unknown, related to τέρμινθος (términthos). The form was perhaps influenced by ἐρέβινθος (erébinthos, “chickpea”).

4408.t: From σμήχω (smḗkhō, “to wipe; to soap off”) + -μα (-mă).

4428.t: From συναναστρέφω (sŭnănăstréphō, “to turn back together, live together”) + -ή (-ḗ).
